info.title: Personalitify API
info.description:
Central backend of the Personalitify ecosystem. Every client — web, the future Rust
desktop application, mobile and third-party integrations — uses this same API.

**Conventions**

- Successful responses are wrapped as `{ "data": …, "meta": … }`.
- Failures are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }`. Branch on
  `code`; `message` is localized from `Accept-Language` (`tr` default, `en`).
- Identifiers are UUID strings. Instants are ISO 8601 in UTC. Calendar dates are
  `YYYY-MM-DD` in the user's time zone. Times of day are `HH:mm`.
- Synchronized resources carry an integer `version`. Send it back as `baseVersion`
  when updating; a stale version is merged field by field or rejected with
  `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`.
- Breaking changes are published under a new path prefix; this document describes
  `/api/v1`.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Data export, security log and account deletion.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Registration, sign-in, token refresh and session management. Access tokens are short-lived JWTs; refresh tokens are opaque, single-use and rotated on every refresh. Browser clients (`clientType: "web"`) receive the refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie; all other clients receive it in the response body.

tags.name: Categories
tags.description: User-defined labels shared by habits, goals, tasks and calendar events.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Client installations registered to the account. A device is registered automatically when it signs in; its id is returned as `tokens.deviceId`.

tags.name: Goals
tags.description: Short- and long-term goals with milestones, sub-goals, reviews and links to habits and tasks. Responses carry a `computed` object with the derived progress.

tags.name: Habits
tags.description: Habits, their schedules and what was recorded for them day by day. Every date is a calendar day in the user’s configured time zone; the server decides what "today" is and reports it in the responses.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness and readiness probes. No authentication.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Preferences that follow the user to every client: language, theme, time zone, date and time formats, notification and privacy preferences.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Tasks with priorities, dates, planned time blocks, subtasks and recurrence. A repeating task is a series of individual tasks: completing one creates the next occurrence.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The signed-in account and its profile.

get.description: Returns every record the account owns, grouped by type, in the same resource format the API uses elsewhere. Credentials and token hashes are never included.

delete.description: Requires the current password. Removes the account and all of its data.

post.description: Creates the account, its profile and settings, registers the device and signs it in. A verification email is sent.

get.summary: Streaks and completion figures of a habit
get.description: Streaks count consecutive completed due days (fixed schedules) or periods that met their quota (flexible schedules). Skipped and postponed days never break a streak; neither does a today that is still open.

extra.description: Completions on days the habit was not due

rate.description: completed / due. Skipped, postponed and still-open days are excluded

put.summary: Record progress, a skip, a postponement or a note for a day
put.description: Creates the entry of that day or updates it. Send `value` for absolute progress or `increment` to add to the stored progress. `status: "skipped"` excuses the day; `status: "postponed"` with `postponedTo` moves the occurrence to a later day.
